items.title: Approval and Adoption of the Minutes
Approval and Adoption of the Minutes
Presentations and Announcements
Steve Thomas, Inspector, Detachment Commander, Wellington County
notes: OPP outlined the organizational chart for the Fergus Detachment. He highlighted the various type of calls responded to as well as the associated increase or decrease in activity. He explained the three occurrence types with the most notable increases from 2021 to 2022 are Break and Enter (30.4), auto thefts (23%) and wildlife strikes (21.5%) Inspector Thomas responded to questions regarding drug and alcohol use, speeding concerns in Belwood and on Black Street in Fergus, reporting traffic complaints through the portal, and data collection through a black cat device.

items.title: Centre Wellington Hydro AGM
notes: Presentation by Wayne Dyce, President

Wayne Dyce, President, Centre Wellington Hydro provided an overview of the group of companies, including their Officers and Directors, Centre Wellington Hydro’s preliminary scorecard, service quality indicators and reliability. He outlined the financial results (revenue, income, dividends), community support, and environmental initiatives.
W. Dyce responded to questions regarding green initiatives funding, EV charging stations, and future expansion of the service area.

items.title: County Council Report - Steve O'Neill, County Councillor Ward 4
notes: County Councillor O’Neill provided highlights including recent speeding enforcement initiatives underway for Belwood, potential installation of speed enforcement cameras, the establishment of the Aboyne Rural Hospice and the purchase of the Catholic School Board administrative offices.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Councillors provided updates regarding participation at the Farm Safety Day, the upcoming Groves Memorial Community Hospital Board, Fergus and Elora BIA initiatives/activities. Mayor Watters indicated he would have an update regarding the Grand River Conservation Authority meeting at the next council meeting.
Councillor Wilton, having declared a conflict of interest with respect to agenda items 8.5 and 8.6 left the meeting.

notes: (RZ05/21) and Geddes/Moir Block, Elora (RZ02/22)

notes: Report from M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer Presentation by Matthew Betik, KPMG re: 2022 Audit Financial Statements

Adam McNabb introduced Matthew Betik, Lead Audit Engagement Partner with KPMG. M. Betik provided an overview of the audit and technology highlights, the status of the audit, significant risks and results as well as other significant findings and results.

items.title: 2024 Budget Directions
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided introductory comments, indicating this is Council’s first opportunity to provide initial direction at the beginning of the budget process. He explained there will be many more opportunities for Members of Council to review and provide input prior to final approval in December. D. Wilson highlighted opportunities for public engagement through a budget survey and delegations and noted corporate business plans that align with the Strategic Plan will form part of the budget.

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report highlighting; Inflation, Asset Management Contribution, Termite Management, Assessment Growth, Fees and Charges, OCIF Funding, Development Charges, 2024 Capital Funding, and the proposed budget schedule.
Staff responded to questions regarding the timing for public consultation, the corporate business plans, the impact of the carbon tax, the timing of new fees and charges and OCIF funding.

notes: Fergus

items.title: Councillor Wilton rejoined the meeting.
notes: Additional Waste Collection in Downtown Areas

Report from K. Drexler, Manager of Community Development K. Drexler, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report, indicating every other week organics collection is a challenge for the businesses and residents in the Fergus and Elora downtown areas. She noted the County has agreed to weekly pick up and staff is recommending the Township pay the additional cost for the weekly pick up to afford the BIAs an opportunity to budget for this service in 2024.

motions.item_title: 2023-45 A By-law to amend the Township of Centre Wellington Zoning
motions.text: THAT By-laws 2023-45 and 2023-46 be read a first, second and third time and passed, signed by the Mayor and Clerk and the Corporate Seal affixed.
motions.text_html: THAT By-laws 2023-45 and 2023-46 be read a first, second and third time and passed, signed by the Mayor and Clerk and the Corporate Seal affixed.

motions.item_title: 2023-45 A By-law to amend the Township of Centre Wellington Zoning
motions.text: THAT By-laws 2023-47 through 2023-52 and 6000-23 be read a first, second and third time and passed, signed by the Mayor and Clerk and the Corporate Seal affixed.
motions.text_html: THAT By-laws 2023-47 through 2023-52 and 6000-23 be read a first, second and third time and passed, signed by the Mayor and Clerk and the Corporate Seal affixed.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington recognizes the need for a balanced approach towards management of short term accommodation rentals within the municipality, and directs staff to explore best practices in other municipalities and report back to Council with recommendations for Centre Wellington to be able to have a program in place by May 1st, 2024.
